rawItems.title: Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan (Referendum Version) Released
rawItems.summary: Ramsey Town Council has published the Referendum Version of the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan for 2026-2046, detailing policies on housing, heritage, environment, and infrastructure for the parish.
rawItems.content: Ramsey Town Council has released the Referendum Version of the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan, covering the period 2026-2046. The plan encompasses the settlements of Ramsey, Ramsey Forty Foot, Ramsey Heights, Ramsey Mereside, Ramsey St Mary's, Ramsey Hollow, and part of Pondersbridge. Produced with support from neighbourhood-plan.co.uk and guided by a steering group led by Sarah Mullineux, the document outlines local planning policies, settlement boundaries, protected spaces, and infrastructure priorities to help shape future development in the parish alongside Huntingdonshire District Council's Local Plan.

rawItems.title: Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan Advances to Referendum
rawItems.summary: The Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan has passed independent assessment and is heading toward a community referendum in December 2026.
rawItems.content: The Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan, prepared following consultations starting in the summer of 2025, has successfully passed Independent Assessment. The next major step will be a community referendum organized by Huntingdonshire District Council, expected in December 2026, where residents on the electoral register will vote on whether to accept the plan. Adoption of the plan will increase Ramsey's share of developer contributions (CIL) from 15% to 25%, providing more funding to be spent directly in the community.

rawItems.title: Abbey College Students Launch Road Safety Campaign for Hollow Lane

rawItems.content: Abbey College students are actively campaigning and raising funds toward the £10,000 required to help pay for speed reduction measures on Hollow Lane. rawItems.title: Ramsey Town Council Discusses Local Plan and Infrastructure

rawItems.content: At the Ramsey Town Council meeting on 10 September 2026, county and district councillors provided updates regarding local roads, the paused Local Government Reorganisation, and the Local Plan 2046. Discussions also covered strategic CIL funding for play parks, the land at Mews Close parking strategy, and the absence of provisions for Traveller and Gypsy sites in the Local Plan.

rawItems.title: Community Praise Following Holme Fen Fires Emergency Response
rawItems.summary: Ramsey Town Council praised the overwhelming community response and local businesses in supporting firefighters during the recent fires at Holme Fen.
rawItems.content: Cllr Fendley provided an update on the operation to support the Fire Service during recent fires at Holme Fen. The Mayor and Town Clerk organised food supplies alongside the Admiral Wells in Holme, and a Go Fund Me page was set up. Volunteers and local businesses provided food over the weekend, leaving firefighters overwhelmed by the community response. Formal letters of thanks are to be issued, and the Chief Fire Officer has been invited to the Mayor's Civic Service in September.

rawItems.title: Abbey College: Weekly Family Update - 13.
rawItems.content: Weekly Family Update - 13.11.26 Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters Most Remembrance Day: A Moment of Unity Remembrance has been marked with great care across our school this week. On Wednesday 11 November, our whole school came together to observe a two-minute silence for Armistice Day. Students who are members of the CCF, other local cadet forces and Scouts also wore their uniforms, adding a special connection to the occasion. items.title: Here is some of Huntingdonshire's most unusual bridges and where to find them
items.content: From a medieval bridge with its own chapel to a 55-arch causeway, Huntingdonshire is packed with unusual crossings. The district’s rivers, floodplains and Fenland waterways have shaped travel for centuries, leaving medieval crossings and Fen drainage bridges behind. Here are some of Huntingdonshire’s most striking bridges and where to find them. St Ives Bridge One of the county’s most extraordinary bridges spans the River Great Ouse at St Ives. The town’s first bridge was built of wood in 1107, before work began on a stone replacement in the early 15th century. The stone crossing was completed in 1425, and a chapel was added the following year. It is one of only three bridges in England with a chapel. The bridge also still bears the scars of the English Civil War. Parliamentary troops destroyed part of it to hinder Royalist forces, so a temporary drawbridge was installed. When the damaged section was rebuilt in 1716, it was given rounded arches instead of matching the pointed medieval ones, leaving a visible difference today. items.title: Hunts man due in court accused of employee theft and fraud offences named
items.content: A Huntingdonshire man is due to appear in court accused of a string of fraud and theft offences. Matthew Stokes, 35, of Liberator Road, Ramsey, is accused of fraud by false representation and theft by an employee. His first hearing is due to take place on November 5 at Cambridge Magistrates' Court. He is alleged to have spent £935.83 on personal items using a company credit card while on leave between August 21 and September 2, knowing the transactions were unauthorised and intending to make financial gain. He is also accused of stealing an Apple iPhone worth £285, a Lenovo laptop worth £478 and several tools, including a drill set. The items belonged to water treatment supplier Prodose Ltd and were allegedly stolen between September 2 and October 14. Between November 13 and December 8, Mr Stokes is accused of stealing tools valued at £2,109.18 from Riverside Waste Machinery Ltd. A further fraud charge alleges that he used or permitted the use of company credit cards for unauthorised transactions totalling £412.41 between October 6 and December 8. All the offences are alleged to have taken place in Huntingdon.

items.title: Plans submitted for four-caravan traveller site on land near Ramsey
items.content: Plans have been submitted to create a new residential traveller site for a family near Ramsey. The application, reference 26/01646/FUL, seeks permission to change the use of land on the south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights, to accommodate four static caravans for residential use. The proposals also include parking for vehicles, space for two touring caravans and the construction of a brick and tile utility and day room for residents. Existing hardstanding at the site would be retained. Applicant Christopher Reilly is seeking permission for the development to provide a permanent home for his family, who are members of the Gypsy and Traveller community. A statement accompanying the plans says: "Mr Reilly and his family are looking for a settled environment with a permanent base to call home."
